tasks.title: Ledger format 4 preserves history and commits alert state with pending deliveries
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, ledger responsibility; R9; R7 delivery-retention compatibility; Counterexamples / Transaction failure and crash recovery (storage guarantees), Alert-state pruning and Ledger format; completion checks 5 and 6. Implement the complete format-4 persistence boundary before wiring evaluation: validated alert_state rows and mirror, read-only validation of format 3, WAL-consistent VACUUM INTO backup through a private temporary file and rename, safe replacement of a backup symlink, existing private wx publish path, direct JSON 1/2 migration to 4, and refusal without changing invalid source files. Keep every channel, mark, payload and recipient record. Expose one batch mutation that atomically stores all alert-row changes (including observed_at-only advances) and missing pending entries with payloads; update memory only after commit and write nothing for an empty batch. Add feed-presence-aware hourly alert-state pruning support, independent of delivery retention, with undefined visibility protecting rows until a good feed read. Use the existing notification type for this storage step; T2 exercises the new payload variants against the same API. Update the exact schema test and add user_version 5 refusal; keep the existing format-3-schema/user_version-4 hostile fixtures in ledger.v2 and index unchanged. Document the migration, backup, private files, pruning and downgrade now. Keep existing lint, typecheck and tests green. Before feature work, capture the config acceptance red baseline below in a writable origin/main scratch checkout, retaining output for T3; do not edit read-only context clones. This establishes the first red check of the spec's TDD order before T2's budget and expiry regressions.

acceptance.expected: Run in the origin/main scratch checkout: nonzero exit with config: unknown key "alerts" in channels[0]. Retain this failing acceptance baseline; parseConfig does not create the output file.

A valid format-3 fixture opens with user_version 4, its backup has user_version 3 and mode 0600, all previous records are equal to the fixture, and a second open has no migration. Invalid format 3, format 4 without alert_state, user_version 5, stage 7 and kind x are refused with source bytes unchanged. A backup symlink's target bytes remain unchanged. A beforeCommit throw leaves 0 added alert rows and 0 added pending entries both in memory and after reopen; successful batch writes survive reopen together, and an observed_at-only change persists. All pruning rows in the spec's table have their literal kept/removed outcomes.

tasks.title: Warning rules produce stable events that every sender can deliver and resend
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, types, pure budget/expiry modules, routing and sender responsibilities; R5-R8 and R10; R9 warning-payload round trips and failed CLI compatibility; Counterexamples / Budget, Expiry, Restart-safe ordering, Routing and config (routing only), and Statistics display examples; completion checks 2 (rule tests), 5 (warning payload persistence) and 6. After the config red baseline, write budget once-per-24-hour tests red first, then expiry [14,3] and the restart-order regression, before implementing the pure functions. Keep each rule's observation selection, transition and key construction together, taking parsed contract types, nowMs and committed stored state as inputs and returning notifications plus proposed state changes. Cover every budget and expiry counterexample, separate check/component identity, strict threshold and boundary times, no recovery reset or downtime burst, freshness and strictly newer observations, observed_at advancement even when stage is unchanged, and rearm only above 14 days. Commit returned changes using T1's ledger in persistence regressions, including the complete restart-safe ordering table. Make Notification an event-discriminated union with unchanged incident fields/JSON and the R8 warning shapes; retain an incident-only event domain for the existing detector/builders so warnings cannot masquerade as incidents. Add the optional channel subscription/control types needed by routing; T3 owns parsing and operational use. Implement opt-in check/component routing without member expansion and independent of sendIncidents. Support all five senders: exact raw webhook/file JSON, signed idempotency, cleaned and escaped chat/email names, warning labels, floor rounding, null availability, singular/zero-day text, status links, hideReason independence and email Message-ID. Prove warning pending/failed payloads survive reopen and failed list/resend works using the existing CLI, which needs no source change. Narrow incident fixture types where the new union requires it without changing old assertions. Add fixtures and warning documentation, including subscription and renewal limits; change only the package description, never pins or dependencies. Keep existing lint, typecheck and tests green. T3 owns HTTP evaluation and the same behavior tests failing on origin/main; missing-module import errors alone do not satisfy the required red evidence.

acceptance.expected: 0 fail in this focused run. At threshold 25: budget 25 produces 0 events and 24.999 produces 1; after an event, +86399999 ms produces 0 more and +86400000 ms produces exactly 1. A check and component sharing id a produce 2 different keys. The expiry sequence 15,14,14,13,4,3,3,2,0,-1 produces exactly [14,3] for both TLS and domain; first observation 2 produces [3]. The six-step restart-order table persists observed_at t0+120000, does not rearm at step 3, emits 0 events at step 4 and exactly 1 milestone-14 event at step 6. Every remaining Budget and Expiry counterexample uses the spec's literal outcome; invalid, stale, equal and reordered readings make no state changes.

acceptance.command: bun test test/message.test.ts test/routing.test.ts test/webhook.test.ts test/failed-cli.test.ts test/channels.test.ts test/ledger.v4.test.ts
acceptance.expected: 0 fail in this focused run. Only subscribed and routed subjects are delivered, exclusions win, and sendIncidents false does not block warning routing. Budget display values 24.96, -3.25 and 99.8816 print 24.9, -3.3 and 99.881 respectively; raw JSON retains the unrounded inputs. All three labels and five sender formats match R8, including no data, 1 day and less than 1 day. Hostile names cannot inject Slack mentions or Teams markup. Webhook idempotency-key equals body key and signing remains valid. Pending and failed warning payloads round-trip unchanged, failed list shows the three event names, and failed resend retains the original key. Existing incident assertions and serialized payloads are unchanged.

acceptance.command: bun run lint && bun run typecheck
acceptance.expected: exit 0; no unsafe casts to fake incident fields, no new runtime dependency, and cognitive complexity at most 15.

tasks.title: Polling sends subscribed warnings durably and all integration and rollout checks pass
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, channel schema/config/index, API feeds/metrics and notifier responsibilities; R1-R4, R9 poll orchestration/pruning and integration of R5-R10; R11; every remaining Counterexample and completion checks 1-10; Performance impact, Security impact and Rollout order. Parse alerts and sendIncidents for all channel types with R1's exact fixed error messages and duplicate handling. Read the integer threshold through kit readInt (fallback 25, min 0, max 100), wire it at startup and preserve stored suppression on edits. Preserve existing Settings equality assertions (for example use a separate threshold reader in config.ts); do not change existing expectations beyond the spec's schema and metrics exceptions. Preserve fetchChecks' existing default public behavior for incident names while collecting additional validated CheckWithState inputs only when alerts are subscribed. Add validated components through the capped, timed, wire-checked, no-redirect client, tolerating 404 without treating it as a good visibility read; update the zero-valued metrics label fixture. Read enabled feeds in parallel, isolate their failures and readiness accounting, and do no additional validation, components request or evaluation without subscriptions. At start, before any resend or held-reminder handling, settle every pending incident or legacy payloadless entry on sendIncidents false channels as dropped; a settle failure never enqueues the key. Keep warning entries pending/resendable, failed incident records unchanged, skip legacy rebuild and seed new automatic/manual incident keys instead of sending them. Preserve first-poll, routing-change and manual seeding, with no replay after re-enable. After per-channel incident/manual processing, gate each warning kind on every subscribing channel having been seeded; evaluate once per installation, atomically commit all proposed alert changes and all routed pending entries in one transaction, and enqueue only after success. Persist every used expiry observation time; retain feed visibility only after good reads for hourly alert-state pruning. Advance suppression even when routing selects no recipient. Keep the reminder stale check narrowed by event. Add HTTP regressions named 'budget once per 24 hours', 'expiry milestones 14 and 3', and 'expiry ordering survives restart', using existing public entrypoints so those same tests fail meaningfully on an origin/main scratch checkout rather than on missing new production-module imports; copy only necessary test fixtures there and retain names/failure lines for the PR. Cover every R4 seeding/subscription table row, R9 rollback/crash/pruning row and R1 sendIncidents table row with literal outcomes, plus all validation/feed failures. Finish R11 docs and the full Security impact checklist. Use only writable scratch copies for origin/main and deploy evidence; context clones and committed deploy image pins remain unchanged. Prepare temporary performance/fake-API harnesses outside the target repository as specified by Performance impact, and set PULSE_571_DEPLOY_SCRATCH to the writable deploy main copy with only its notify image replaced by pulse-notify:candidate. The final PR owns complete red/green, security, performance, manual-run, Compose and green-CI evidence, names the allowed expectation changes, the unchanged hostile user_version-4 cases and the added user_version-5 case, and lists every known limit in completion check 10.

Run five times on origin/main and five times on the branch on the same machine; all ten full suites pass. Report every user/system pair, both medians of user+system seconds and their difference; branch minus main is strictly below 0.3 s, the literal local A/B limit in Performance impact.

Runtime: 200 checks (100 HTTP, 50 TLS, 50 domain), 50 components, fresh per-request timestamps, 1000-ms polling, 20-s warm-up and a 60-s measurement for main, branch without alerts and branch with all three alerts. Report /proc CPU, VmRSS and VmHWM for all three; branch-without-alerts minus main is at most 0.1 s CPU and 3 MiB VmHWM, and branch-with-alerts minus main is at most 0.3 s CPU and 3 MiB VmHWM.
